questions.question: A fair coin is tossed and a fair six-sided die is rolled. What is the probability of getting a head and a 4?
questions.explanation: P(head) = 1/2. P(4) = 1/6. Since events are independent: P(head and 4) = 1/2 x 1/6 = 1/12.

questions.question: Two fair coins are tossed. What is the probability of getting two heads?
questions.explanation: P(head on first coin) = 1/2. P(head on second coin) = 1/2. P(both heads) = 1/2 x 1/2 = 1/4.

questions.question: The probability that Ali passes a test is 0.8 and the probability that Ben passes the same test is 0.7. If their results are independent, what is the probability that both pass?
questions.explanation: For independent events: P(both pass) = P(Ali passes) x P(Ben passes) = 0.8 x 0.7 = 0.56.

questions.question: A bag contains 3 red balls and 2 blue balls. A ball is drawn, replaced, and another ball is drawn. What is the probability of getting two red balls?
questions.explanation: With replacement, events are independent. P(red) = 3/5. P(two reds) = 3/5 x 3/5 = 9/25.

questions.question: Which condition must be true for two events to be independent?
options: P(A and B) = P(A) x P(B)
P(A or B) = P(A) x P(B)
questions.explanation: Two events A and B are independent if and only if P(A and B) = P(A) x P(B). The occurrence of one does not affect the other.

questions.question: A fair die is rolled twice. What is the probability of getting a 6 on the first roll and an even number on the second roll?
questions.explanation: P(6 on first) = 1/6. P(even on second) = 3/6 = 1/2. P(both) = 1/6 x 1/2 = 1/12.

questions.question: The probability that it rains on Saturday is 0.3 and on Sunday is 0.4. Assuming independence, what is the probability that it rains on both days?
questions.explanation: P(rain both days) = P(rain Sat) x P(rain Sun) = 0.3 x 0.4 = 0.12.

questions.question: A spinner has 4 equal sections: red, blue, green, yellow. If the spinner is spun twice, what is the probability of getting red both times?
questions.explanation: P(red) = 1/4. P(red both times) = 1/4 x 1/4 = 1/16.

questions.question: The probability that Ali passes is 0.8. What is the probability that Ali fails?
Using the previous question, if Ali takes two independent tests each with 0.8 probability of passing, what is the probability he passes both?
questions.explanation: P(pass both) = 0.8 x 0.8 = 0.64.

questions.question: A fair coin is tossed 3 times. What is the probability of getting 3 heads?
questions.explanation: P(head) = 1/2 for each toss. P(3 heads) = 1/2 x 1/2 x 1/2 = 1/8.

questions.question: A fair die is rolled 3 times. What is the probability of getting a 6 on all three rolls?
questions.explanation: P(6) = 1/6 for each roll. P(three 6s) = 1/6 x 1/6 x 1/6 = 1/216.

questions.question: The probability that machine A works is 0.9 and machine B works is 0.8. If they operate independently, what is the probability that both machines work?
questions.explanation: P(both work) = P(A works) x P(B works) = 0.9 x 0.8 = 0.72.

questions.question: Using the machines from the previous question, what is the probability that both machines fail?
A bag contains 4 red and 6 blue balls. A ball is drawn, replaced, then another is drawn. What is the probability of getting one red and one blue in that order?
questions.explanation: P(red first) = 4/10 = 2/5. P(blue second) = 6/10 = 3/5. P(red then blue) = 2/5 x 3/5 = 6/25 = 24/100.

questions.question: Two cards are drawn from a standard deck of 52 cards with replacement. What is the probability of drawing two kings?
questions.explanation: P(king) = 4/52 = 1/13. With replacement: P(two kings) = 1/13 x 1/13 = 1/169.

questions.question: The probability that a student is late on any day is 0.1. What is the probability that the student is late on Monday and Tuesday (assuming independence)?
questions.explanation: P(late Mon and Tue) = 0.1 x 0.1 = 0.01.

questions.question: Using the previous question, what is the probability that the student is on time for both Monday and Tuesday?
questions.explanation: P(on time) = 1 - 0.1 = 0.9. P(on time both days) = 0.9 x 0.9 = 0.81.

questions.question: Event A has probability 0.6 and event B has probability 0.5. If A and B are independent, what is P(A and B)?
questions.explanation: For independent events: P(A and B) = P(A) x P(B) = 0.6 x 0.5 = 0.30.

questions.question: A target shooter has a 0.7 probability of hitting the target on each shot. What is the probability of hitting the target on the first two shots?
Using the previous question, what is the probability that the shooter misses both shots?
A box contains 5 defective items out of 20. Two items are selected with replacement. What is the probability both are defective?
questions.explanation: P(defective) = 5/20 = 1/4. P(both defective) = 1/4 x 1/4 = 1/16.

questions.question: The probability of getting a head on a biased coin is 0.6. If the coin is tossed twice, what is P(at least one head)?
questions.explanation: P(no heads) = P(tail) x P(tail) = 0.4 x 0.4 = 0.16. P(at least one head) = 1 - 0.16 = 0.84.

questions.question: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that both show a number less than 3?
questions.explanation: Numbers less than 3: 1 and 2. P(less than 3) = 2/6 = 1/3. P(both less than 3) = 1/3 x 1/3 = 1/9.

questions.question: If P(A) = 0.4, P(B) = 0.5, and A and B are independent, what is P(A' and B)?
questions.explanation: P(A') = 1 - 0.4 = 0.6. Since A and B are independent, A' and B are also independent. P(A' and B) = 0.6 x 0.5 = 0.30.
